function: Learns the BS downlink beamforming function (continuous current distribution over the CAPA) with implicit neural networks, directly (BeaINR) or via a weighting coefficient function (CoefINR), maximizing SE (pp. 1-4).
system: Downlink MIMO with continuous aperture arrays at BS (2x2 m) and user (0.5x0.5 m), line-of-sight, N=min(M_B,M_U) streams, 2.4 GHz, no RIS (pp. 2, 4-5).
method: Two fully connected networks (implicit neural representations), unsupervised training with negative SE loss, integrals by Gauss-Legendre and Sobol sampling; CoefINR exploits the optimal beamforming structure (pp. 3-5).
data_channel: Self-generated: 500,000 training and 10,000 test samples with random user positions; analytic line-of-sight CAPA channel response of Eq. (3); no public dataset or measurement (pp. 2, 4-5).
test_conditions: Train: A_B 4 m2, A_U 0.5 m2, 2.4 GHz, rz 20-30 m. Test: A_B 2-6 m2, A_U 0.3-0.7 m2, 1.8-3 GHz, larger user region (pp. 5-6).
baselines: Non-learned: WMMSE (calculus of variations), Fourier-basis optimization, SPDA discretization with SVD and water-filling. No earlier learned method; only BeaINR and CoefINR (p. 5).
metrics: Spectral efficiency, SE ratio to WMMSE (%), inference time, training samples, time and space, SE under amplitude and phase quantization (Figs. 2-4, Tables I-III, pp. 5-6).
complexity: Measured inference time 0.062 s (BeaINR) and 0.043 s (CoefINR) versus 0.378 s for WMMSE; training 25K samples, 36.2 h vs 20K samples, 3.68 h (Table III, p. 6).
q1_support: p. 2: "we consider unipolarized CAPAs under line-of-sight conditions"; the channel h(r, s) is the analytic free-space response of Eq. (3), a custom model with no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 5: "both models are trained with AB = 4 m2 and tested over" 2-6 m2; also trained at 2.4 GHz and tested over 1.8-3 GHz (p. 5), and tested on a larger user region than in training (p. 6).
q3_support: p. 5: "We compare the learning performance of BeaINR and CoefINR against the following numerical baselines"; WMMSE, Fourier and SPDA are all non-learned, and no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 6: "Table III compares the inference time and training complexity of the considered methods"; inference time 0.062 s (BeaINR) and 0.043 s (CoefINR), training 36.2 h and 3.68 h.
q5_support: p. 4: "For training, we generate 500,000 samples"; the data are self-generated from Eq. (3) and the paper gives no code or data link, DOI or public dataset.
notes: Step 1: research letter on learned downlink beamforming for continuous aperture arrays (CAPAs) at the BS and the user (p. 1); not a survey; a neural network performs the beamforming (p. 3), so area 3. Not a single-antenna link: N = min(M_B, M_U) streams between two CAPAs (p. 4). A CAPA is an antenna technology, not a RIS, so ris = 0. q3 = 0 because both learned methods are the paper's own and its three baselines are non-learned (p. 5). Perfect CSI is assumed (p. 2). Minor inconsistency in the paper: the setup gives a 0.5 m x 0.5 m user CAPA (p. 4) while the generalization test says training with A_U = 0.5 m2 (p. 5). The PDF is the arXiv 2507.03609v3 preprint (p. 1).
